# Code Quality

## Anti-defaults (counter common Claude tendencies)

- No premature abstractions. Three similar lines beat a helper used once.
- Don't add features or improvements beyond what was asked.
- Don't refactor adjacent code while fixing a bug.
- No dead code or commented-out blocks; git keeps the history.
- Comment WHY, never WHAT. If code needs a "what" comment, rename instead.
- Document the API at module boundaries only, not on every internal function.

## Naming

Match the convention of the surrounding code rather than imposing a universal rule.

- **Booleans**: prefix with `is` / `has` / `should` / `can`. **Functions**: verb-first.
- **Factories**: `create*` / `make_*`. **Converters**: `to*`. **Predicates**: `is*`.
- Use abbreviations only when they're universally known (`id`, `url`, `api`, `db`, `auth`).
- Wire-format and external identifiers (protobuf fields, API JSON keys, DB columns) keep their on-the-wire spelling verbatim — don't rename them to match local style.

## Code Markers

Use `TODO(author): desc (#issue)` for planned work, `FIXME(author): desc (#issue)` for known bugs, `HACK(author): desc (#issue)` for ugly workarounds (explain the proper fix), and `NOTE: desc` for non-obvious context. An owner and issue link are required. Never use `XXX`, `TEMP`, or `REMOVEME`.

## File Organization

- Group imports (stdlib, third-party, internal, relative) with a blank line between groups; follow the project's formatter.
- One public class or component per file, unless they're tightly related.
- Order functions with the public API first, then helpers in call order.
